newsitem.title: CANADA: CAW boss to meet Canada minister on CAI.
newsitem.headline: CAW boss to meet Canada minister on CAI.

text.p: Canadian Auto Workers union president Buzz Hargrove was in Ottawa on Wednesday for a meeting with Canadian Transport Minister David Anderson to discuss the fate of cash-strapped Canadian Airlines Corp, Transport Canada and CAW spokesmen said.
Neither office was able to give details of where or when the meeting would occur.
Five of the troubled airline's six unions have agreed to a tough restructuring program, including wage cuts, in an effort to save the money-losing carrier.
The CAW, representing about 3,700 of Canadian's 16,400 employees, is the only union that has refused to endorse the restructuring plan, calling instead for a government bailout for the airline.

But Ottawa has repeatedly refused to provide a cash bailout for Canadian, offering instead a fuel tax rebate that would save Canadian C$35 million a year. The government also agreed to extend repayment of C$30 million in loans to Canadian by 12 to 18 months.
The company's proposed wage cuts would save a further C$35 million.
Canadian, which has not posted a yearly profit in about a decade, could cease operations by early next year if it failed to find a way to deal with its C$2.8 billion of debt and lease obligations.
Fort Worth-based AMR Corp, the parent of American Airlines, has a 33 percent ownership stake and 25 percent voting interest in Canadian Airlines International, the operating unit of Canadian.
On Tuesday, AMR agreed to cut its service fees by C$48 million a year over four years to support Canadian's restructuring.
